items.stem: What best distinguishes strategic leadership from day-to-day management?

options.text: Setting direction and enabling change versus organising existing work well
options.rationale: Correct: leadership sets direction and drives change; management executes and coordinates current work.

options.text: Leadership is only about giving orders
options.rationale: Leadership is about direction and influence, not merely commands.
Management involves substantial planning and coordination.
They overlap but are distinct; the distinction is the point.

items.explanation: Correct: leadership centres on direction and change, management on executing current work.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve decision-making under uncertainty? (Select TWO)

options.text: Judging decisions by their process quality, not only outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: good processes matter because outcomes are partly luck under uncertainty.

options.text: Stress-testing a choice against multiple scenarios
options.rationale: Correct: scenarios reveal how robust a decision is to different futures.

options.text: Avoiding any decision until all uncertainty is removed
options.rationale: Waiting for certainty is usually impossible and costly.

options.text: Rewarding only decisions that happened to succeed
options.rationale: Outcome-only judgement ignores decision quality and luck.

items.explanation: Correct: focusing on process quality and testing scenarios both strengthen decisions under uncertainty.

items.stem: Why can a well-formulated strategy still fail?

options.text: Execution, alignment and change management are neglected
options.rationale: Correct: strategy delivers value only when resources, incentives and people are aligned to execute it.
Formulation matters; the point is that execution also matters.
Measures help; neglecting them is a cause of failure, not measures themselves.
Ignoring stakeholders increases, not reduces, the risk of failure.

items.explanation: Correct: strategies fail when execution, alignment and change are neglected.
